failure_modes_surfaced.description: Database is unreachable or times out during user lookup
failure_modes_surfaced.resolution: Return 500; handled before password check step

failure_modes_surfaced.description: Distinguishing no-user from wrong-password without leaking enumeration
Returning 'user not found' specifically leaks which emails are registered
failure_modes_surfaced.resolution: Same generic error message for all authentication failures

failure_modes_surfaced.description: Manually hashing input then comparing will fail because bcrypt salts are embedded in the stored hash
No rate limiting means an attacker can send unlimited login attempts
failure_modes_surfaced.resolution: Per-email attempt counter in Redis with lockout threshold; 429 on breach

engineer_growth_signals: Independently identified user enumeration risk when prompted about the error message
Independently identified bcrypt.compare after a Socratic hint about bcrypt mechanics
Reasoned through rate-limiting placement tradeoffs and gave a justified decision
issues_found: Engineer's initial flow had no failure modes at all — 4 out of 5 failure modes required prompting
Engineer initially dismissed DB failure as 'not my problem to handle' — required one redirect question
